content.value_statement: Structural changes can leave project documentation incomplete or contradictory. This skill identifies affected documents and keeps durable decisions aligned with the code.
actual_capabilities: Detects changes that affect architecture, UX standards, quality gates, workflows, or cross-cutting conventions.
Maps change types to README.md, DESIGN.md, AGENTS.md, or docs/adr/.
Checks which candidate documents exist before recommending edits.
Keeps each fact in one document and links to it from related documents.
Guides ADR creation with numbering, required sections, and supersession rules.
Produces an output list of updated, created, or deliberately skipped documents.
limitations: It does not edit documents unless the host agent applies its recommendations.
It cannot verify code behavior beyond the context provided by the host agent.
It does not replace repository-specific contribution or ADR conventions.
It creates an ADR only when the decision has durable impact and real alternatives.

use_cases.title: Record an architecture change
use_cases.description: Identify affected project documents and update the architecture record without duplicating the same fact across files.

use_cases.title: Maintain interface standards
use_cases.description: Route visual or UX changes to the correct design documentation and check that guidance matches the implementation.

use_cases.title: Document operational decisions
use_cases.description: Update workflow guidance or create a numbered ADR when a durable operational decision has meaningful alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Find affected documents
prompt_templates.prompt: A new structural change was made: [describe change]. Identify the existing project documents that require review and explain why.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: locate documentation affected by a change.

prompt_templates.title: Sync a design decision
prompt_templates.prompt: The interface standard changed: [describe standard]. Classify the change, identify existing files to update, and list the required edits.

prompt_templates.title: Plan an ADR
prompt_templates.prompt: We chose [decision] over [alternatives] because [context]. Determine whether an ADR is warranted and draft its required sections.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: capture a durable decision with consequences.

prompt_templates.title: Audit documentation consistency
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this structural change and the provided documentation: [change and excerpts]. Find contradictions, assign each fact to one source document, and report skipped files with reasons.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: reconcile documentation against a code change.

output_examples.input: A repository introduced a shared component standard and updated its design tokens.
output: Update DESIGN.md with the token and component rules.
Review README.md only if the standard changes repository structure.
Skip AGENTS.md because the change does not alter agent workflow.

output_examples.input: A team selected a queue-based integration after comparing two alternatives.
output_examples.output: Create the next numbered ADR with Status, Context, Decision, and Consequences. Link related documentation to the ADR instead of repeating the decision.

best_practices: Check document existence before proposing edits.
Keep each durable fact in one authoritative document.
Reread edited sections against the current code.
anti_patterns: Do not duplicate the same decision across multiple documents.
Do not rewrite an accepted ADR when a new decision supersedes it.
Do not create an ADR for a local feature change without durable alternatives.

faq.question: What changes activate this skill?
faq.answer: Architecture, UX standards, quality gates, agent workflows, and cross-cutting conventions activate this skill.

faq.question: Which documents does it manage?
faq.answer: It maps changes to README.md, DESIGN.md, AGENTS.md, and docs/adr/ when those paths exist.

faq.question: Does it always create an ADR?
faq.answer: No. It creates an ADR only for a durable decision with meaningful alternatives and consequences.

faq.question: How does it avoid duplicate facts?
faq.answer: It assigns each fact to one authoritative document and links to that document from related files.

faq.question: Can it rewrite an accepted ADR?
faq.answer: No. A superseding ADR should record the new decision, and the older record should receive a status update.

faq.question: What does the final report include?
faq.answer: The report lists every document updated, created, or deliberately skipped, with a reason for each result.
